THE PROPOSED EXTENSION OF THE
INFIRMARY.

A meeting of the Board of Management of this Institution was held yesterday afternoon, Alder- man Davies presiding, to further consider the scheme for extending the accommodation. The minutes of the Medical Committee, together with a preliminary report by Mr. W. Owen, were read and discussed,, after which it was.resolved,on the motion of the Rev. J. Yonge, seconded by Mr. J. White, "that the proposals of the Medical Committee be favourably entertained,and that a special committee be appointed for the consideration. of the scheme and details, and to report to a *future meeting, ' such Corrunittee toconsist of the honorary medical officers, and Aldermen Joseph Davies, Major Litton, Mr. Monks,, Mr. Crwen, and Mr. J. L. Tunstall.'rlir. Davies suggested that the movement should be con- nected with the intended memorial tb the late- Mr. Bearaont, who *as chairman of the Board of Man- agement, and the suggestion seemed to meet with the approbation of those present.

CHRISTMAS TREE AND SALE OF Woe.—On Tuesday afternoon a sale of work was opened in the sc/molroom of the United Methodist Free Church, Frodsliam, by Mr. T. Arthur Rigby, of Overton, th• object being to raise funds to clear off the debt, amounting to nearly £lOO, which remained on the chapel premises. The Rev. J. Shipham (Wesleyan) proposed, and the Rev. fl. Davenport (Primitive) seconded,a vote of thanks to Mr. Rigby for his service,s,and the sale was then commenced.. The amount realized was over £3O.

div.head: ENTERTAINM- ENT OF CLASSES.
div.p: ENTERTAINM- ENT OF CLASSES.

On Wednesday evening the members of Miss Lily Routledge's juvenile class, along with the members of Miss Emma Hobson's Stinday School class, met together in the Wesleyan schoolroom, at the invit- ation of Miss L Routledge, to, a social tea party. After ta all kinds of games were indulged in, and a very pleasant evening was, spent and heartily appreciated by all. SOIREE AT THE CONSERVATIVE CLUB. In connection with the Conservative Club dancing class, a soiree was held on Saturday evening. About 50 persons were present, and the dancing was kept up until a late hour with much vigour. Re- frahtnents were supplied in abundance by "Mrs. Peter Pownall, Miss Emily Boardman, and Mi4s4 E. Boardman. Mr. John Parks officiated as M.C4'.iind the meeting was a thorough success. WATCH NIGHT. Oa Tuesday evening the annual tea party and entertainment were held in connection with the Penketh Wesleyan Chapel watch night services. About eighty persons sat down ton substantial tea, which was provided by Mrs. R. Garnett, ably assisted by Misses A. Moses and L. Routledge. After tea an interesting programme was gone through, consisting of selections - from "A Day with bur Lord" by a number of friends, and other stings' &c. Mr. R. Garnett presided. The Chairman, the Rev. E. 11. Jackson, Mr. R. Cook, Mr. Carr (of New York), and Mr. C. E. Parker addressed the meeting. Mr. Cook mentioned that it was intended to enlarge the chapel at a cost of about £4OO. At a quarter to eleven the watch night service was coMmenCed, conducted by Rev. E. H. Jackson, and it lasted until the clock passed midnight, and the new year was ushered in.
I

OLD FOLKS' TREAT. Last night, this annual event, which originated clurrng the Jubilee year, came off at the Conservati vP Club-room. There weni.present between 60 and 70 of the poor of Penketh, their ages varying from 50 to 75 years. After tea, oranges, apples, and tobacco, were distributed. The Committee "con- sisted of the following gentlemen :—Messrs. J. C. Routledge. Chairman; Jonas Foster, Secretary; James Jackson, R. Boardman, T. H. Wilson, Peter Boardman, W. 'Longshaw, and W. Hough. Mesdames Routledge; Longshaw, Boardman, Misses Thorpe and Forster had the management of the VA. The room was nicely decorated for the occa- sion with banners, evergreens. etc. A capital pro- gramme of ssngs; recitations, &c., was given by the following :—Mr. White, Miss Lily Rutledge, Mr.

Rook, Mrs. Guy, Miss Marian Forster, Mr. Denton, Messrs. E. L. and F. Forster, Miss Katie Entwistle, Sergeant Donoghue, Mr. Watler, and Mr. J. Main- ley. During the evening various speeches were given. At the close the women were each supplied with a quarter pound of tea, and the men with tobacco and a pipe.

div.head: WARRINGTON TOWN COUNCIL.
div.p: WARRINGTON TOWN COUNCIL.

A meeting' of this Council will be held, at the ToWn Hall on Tuesday evening next. Sal4crloN OF LOAN.—The Finance Committee will report that the Local Government Board have sanc- tioned the borrowing of £6,954 for the purpose of making additions to andalterations at the depots. THE CONTESTED VICECHAIRMANSHIP"— Th e Town Hall,Park arid Baths Committee's minutes will contain a resolution that that portion of the minute of the 14th November last, viz. :--" That Mr. Coun- cillor Bolton be appointed the deputy-chairman of the Committee for the ensuing year;" be again sub- mitted to the 'Council for approval. TEE GAS ANNUITANTS. —Th e General Purposes Com- mittee will recommend that the Town Clerlrbe instructod to give notice to the gas annuitants,. that the latter part of section 177 of the proposed Bill,relating to the compul- sory redemption of the annuities at 25 years' purchase, will be withdrawn in Committee of the House. PREPARING FOR EMERGENCIES .—The Fire Engine Committee have passed a resolution that application be made to the Warrington Waterworks Company to fix six hydrants on the new main now Doing laid in Knots- ford-road, Latchford.

COUNTY OF LANCASTER. THE CONTAGIOUS DISEASES (ANIMALS) ACT, 1878 AND 1886. TILE RABIES (MUZZLING OF DOGS) ORDER OF 1889. BY THE BOARD OF AGRICULTURE. THE Board of Agriculture, by virtue and In'-exercise of the powers in them vested under The Board of Agriculture Act, 1889, and The Contagious Diseases (Animals) Acts, 1878 to 1866 and of every other power enabling them in this behalf, do order, and it is hereby ordered, as follows: SHORT TITLE. 1. This Order may be cited as Tax RABIES (MUZZLING OF DOGS) ORDER OF 1889. EXTENT AND ENFORCEMENT. 2. This Order applies to and Shall be in force in the dics- tricts of the Local Authorities mentioned in the Schedule to this Order, and to any other District or part of a District of a Local Authority to which this Order may at any time be applied by any further Order of the Board of Agriculture. and shall be enforced by each of such Local Authorities whhin their District. COMMENCEMENT AND DURATION. 3. This Order shall commence and take effect from and immediately after the thirty-first day of December, one thou- sand eight hundred and eighty-nine ; and shall continue to have effect and to apply to each of the Districts mentiated to the Schedule to this Order until this Order is declared by further Order of the Board to cease to apply to such District. INTERPRETATION. 4. In this Order— • Public place includes any street. highway, thoroughfare, , public bridge, roSral park, public park garden ,or pleasure ground, common, uninclosed land, or other place to tvhielt ' the public have for the time being access : The Act 01 1878 means The Contagious Diseolor (Animals) , Act, 1878 ; Other terms have the same meaning as in the Rabies Order of 1887. SLAUGHTER OF DOGS AFFECTED WITH OR SUSPECTED OF RABIES. 5. The Local Authority shall cause all dogs affected with or suspected of rabies or having been bitten by a dog affected with or suspected of rabies within their District to be forth- with slaughtered. MUZZLING OF DOGS. 6.—(1.) No dog shall be allowed to be in or on any public place unless such dog is muzzled with a muzzle so constructed as to render it impossible for such dog while wearing the same to Oil c arty coatcoal., be:- not so as dog from breathing freely or lapping water. (2.) If any dog is found in or on any public place without being muzzled in manner prescribed by this Article, the person for the time being in charge of the dog, and the owner thereof, and the person allowing the same to be in or on such public place in contravention of this Article, shall, each according to and in respect of his own acts and defaults, be deemed guilty of an offence against the Act of 1878. (3.) Providedthat the provisions of this Article shall not apply to— (a) Packs of hounds or greyhounds while being exercised or used for sporting purposes, or other sporting dogs, while being used for sporting purposes, or any dogs while being used for the capture or destruction of vermin, and in every case in charge of competent persons. (5) Dogs while being taken to or from Exhibitions. Shows or other places if raid: dogs are confined in boxes, cages, crates baskets or hampers so constructed as to render It impossible for such dogs while so confined to bite any persou or animal. SEISURE, DETENTION, AND DISPOSAL OF STRAY DOGS AND OF DOGS NOT MUZZLED. 7. The Lo-al Authority,shall cause all stray dogs, and all dogs not muzzled ln accordance with the provisions of this Order, found within their District, to be seised, and such dogs so seised shall be dealt withas follows (i.) If the dog is affected with, or suspected of, rabies it shall be forthwith slaughtered. , (11.) If the dog is not affected with, or suspected of, rabies it shall be detained in some proper place and be there kept for such period as the Local Authority think expedient: Pro- vided that where the person having charge of or the owner of a dog so detained is known, the Local Authority shall cause uctice to be forthwith given to such person or owner of the fact of the clog having been so seised and detained, and the dog shall, without prejudice to the recovery of any penalty for the infringement of this Order, be given up to such per- son or owner on payment of the reasonable expenses incurred by the Local Authority in respect of such detention. (iii.) lithe dog 80 seised and detained has not been claimed by such person or owner within three days after the seisure, or where such person or owner is known within two, days after the aforesaid notice has been given, the Local Authority may cause the dog to be slaughtered or otherwise disposed of ha such manner as the Local Authority deem expedient. FOOD AND WATER DURING DETENTION. 8. A Local Authority, or an Inspector, officer, or constable detaining a dog under this Order shall cause it to be supplied with requisite tood and water during its detention ; and the expenses incurred by the Local Authority, or by the Inspec- tor, officer, or constable in respect thereof may be recovered summarily by the Local Authority from the perscin having. charge of the dog or from its owner. EXPENSES OF LOCAL AUTHORITY. 9.—(1.) All expenses incurred in respect of the seisure or detention of any dog under the authority of this Order shall be defrayed by the Local Authority within whose District, the dog wee seised and such expenses and all other expenses incurred in carrying out the provisions of this Order shall be expenses of the Local Authority for the purposes of the Act of 1878. (2.) A Local Authoiity, in any case where a dog is detained under the provisions of this Order, may recover summarily from the person having charge of the dog or from its owner the expenses incurred in respect of the detention of such dog. TEMPORARY SUSPENSION OF LOCAL AUTHORITY'S SPECIAL REGULATIONS As TO' DOGS. ' 10. The operation of any Regulationmade by a Local Authority under Article 12 of The Rabies Order of 1887 (Special Regulations of Local Authority as to Dogs) or under Article 10 of the Rabies Order of 1886 and continued by the sold Order of 1887, or under The Rabies (Amendment) Order of 1889, is berebY, so far as ally such Regulation may be applicable to ally District to which this Order applies, sus- pended for the period during which this Order applies to such District. GENERAL PROVISIONS OF THE RABIES ORDER or 1887. 11. Subject to the last foregoing Article of this Order, all the provisions of The Rabies Order of 1887 shall, so far as the same are applicable, continue to apply, during thecontinuance of this Order, to the Districts to yr hich this Order applies. In yvitness whereof the Board of Agriculture have here- unto set their OfficiAl Seal this seventeenth day of , December, one thousand eight hundred and eighty- nine. G. A. BOTELER GRAMMAR SVHOOL, WARRINGTON. POUNDED A.D. 1526. Head Masters The Rev. E. J. WILLCOCKS, M.A., Late Scholar at St. Catherine's College, Cambridge. Second Master The Rev. 11. G. SMITH, M.A., Scholar of St. John's College, Cambridge; And five Assistant Masters. The School contains two divisions. The work of the Lower Division comprises a regular course of instruction in English, French. the rudiments of Latin, elemerftary Mathematics and Science, with Reading, Writing, Arithmetic, Drawing, Drill, and Vocal Music, and all other elements of a sound modern education. In the Upper Division, the choice is offered of a thorough mercantile or high classical course; German and Greek being optional subjects. Twelve Free Scholarships. Two Exhibitions to Oxford and Cambridge. The year is divided into three Terms. Capitation Fees, everything included, £4 and £3 per term in the Upper and Lower Divisions respectively. Entrance Fee. £l. Next Term begins on Tuesday, January 21st, 1890.

THE SHIP CANAL, A WORD FOR THE NAVVIES. A man who was charged with felony, before the magis- trates at Warrington on Saturday, described himself as a Ship Canal navvy, and the Chief Constable (Mr. Hunt) remarked that a great many people who came to War- rington and got into trouble incorrectly said that they were navvies, because it was convenient to do so. He believed that the great majority of the Ship Canal navvies were honest men. MORRISBROOK TEMPERANCE SOCIETY. The opening meeting of this society was held in the Thelwall Mission Hall, on Monday evening. The Hon. and Rev. Mr. Grimston took the chair, and spoke bf the necessity of introducing temperance amongst the work- men on the canal. He said that great good had been done in that direction on some sections of the canal, and he expressed a hope that similar results would follow on that section. The Chairman then called upon Mr. Manning to explain the constitution of the society. In the course of his remarks the last-named gentleman urged upon those present the need of fidelity to their temperance principles. An interesting address was also given by Mr. G. A. Wray, C.E.T.S. temperance lecturer for the county of Kent. It may be mentioned that Mr. H. Price is secretary of the new society, and Mr. Manning assistant secretary. THELWALL MISSION HALL. During the week there have been special prayer meet- ings in the Mission Hall, at Thelwall, and on New Year's Eve there was a watch-night service at which an address on "Memory" was given by Mr. Manning. Special services will be held during next week at the Mission Hall. WORK ON THE CANAL. The recent frosts have stopped work to a great extent on the canal, but the preliminary work in connection with the erection of the railway bridge over the canal near Latchford locks is still being carried on. During the holidays there have been many visitors to the canal in the neighbourhood of the locks and Thelwall, some of these coming from great distances. The excellent refreshment rooms on the canal between Thelwall and Morris Brook are evidently found to be a great conveni- ence to visitors to that neighbourhood.

FATAL ICE ACCIDENT. A boy named Taylor was drowned at a reservoir called Doffcocker's Lodge, near Bolton, on Thursday evening, by falling through thin ice. A WINDFALL. A Guildford telegram states that a blacksmith named Barber, living at Albury, near that town, has just received a "windfall" of £lO,OOO. LONGTON COLLIERY DISASTER. At five o'clock on Thursday morning the 5/3th body was recovered from the Mossfield Colliery, where the disas- trous explosion took place on the 16th October. De- ceased was Job Bull. of Anchor-road, Sandford Hill. SINGULAR DRCWNING CASE. Yesterday morning the Preston District Coroner re- ceived information of the drowning of two boys in the canal at Appleby Bridge, Upholland, near Wigan. It is supposed they were riding a donkey which has the habit of backing, and had backed into the canal with them. SPANISH MINISTERIAL CRISIS. A Ministerial cesis exists at Madrid. Senor Sag,asta has tendered to the Queen Regent hi 3 resignation, and that of his Ministerial colleagues. Senor Sega.sta will endeavonr to form a new Cabinet .on the basis of a reconciliation between the different groups of the Liberal party. THE GAS STRIKE IN LONDON. Yesterday the South Metropolitan Gas Company issued to their consumers circulars thanking them for economizing gas during the strike. The company have withdrawn the gratuity to the men who remained with them, commencing with next week. A BRIGANTINE SUNK IN COLLISION. A CAPTAIN DROWNED. A collision occurred off the Mersey on Thursday night between the White Star steamer Britannic and the brigantine Czarowitz, from Fowey to Runcorn. The brigantine sank almost immediately, and John Pengelly, the captain, who was drowned, was heard to say when she was struck, " She's done for now." The remainder of the crew took to the rigging and were rescued.
